items.title: Thanksgiving Storm Aftermath, Black Friday Economy, Eisenkot's Coalition Talks
items.summary: Powerful storms left nearly a million customers without power on Thanksgiving and disrupted travel across much of the country, but conditions are expected to improve heading into the weekend. Americans are expected to spend a record amount this holiday season, even as inflation forces many shoppers to cut back on other expenses to afford gifts. Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot could unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as early as next week, but divisions among his potential coalition partners could make it difficult to keep a new government together.

items.title: Feeling more anxious? Researchers may know what’s driving it
items.summary: Younger people are more anxious these days than previous generations, and scientists have speculated all kinds of reasons as to why. A new study pinpoints when anxiety started rising – about 15 years ago. That aligns with when many people started amping up their smartphone use. But what about phones is making people more anxious? The answer may surprise you: Researchers think it may have to do with the way we handle uncertainty. If you liked this episode, check out our episode on the science of healthy screen time . Interested in more science in the news? Email us your question at shortwave@npr.org .

items.title: Zelensky criticises 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
items.summary: Ukraine's president voices frustration with US and says it is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks to end the war.
items.body: Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, criticising Donald Trump for calling Vladimir Putin "my friend" and saying delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles were costing Ukrainian lives.

items.title: Leaders clash in final Spain election debate as housing dominates run-in
items.summary: The struggle many face in buying a home has been the biggest issue of a bitter campaign.
items.body: Spain's main party leaders have made their last pitch to voters in a fractious final TV debate that focused heavily on the country's housing crisis. Spaniards go to the ballot box on Sunday, with opinion polls suggesting Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez will fail to extend his eight years in office.

items.title: Mushroom murderer Erin Patterson launches last-ditch High Court appeal
items.summary: Erin Patterson is serving life in prison for poisoning her relatives with a toxic mushroom lunch in 2023.
items.body: Australia's mushroom killer Erin Patterson has launched a final legal bid to overturn her murder convictions and avoid dying in jail. Patterson, 52, was last year found guilty of murdering three relatives and attempting to kill another when she served them a toxic mushroom-laced meal in 2023.

items.title: Mad about mara: the DIY dance movement helping young Nigerians escape the daily grind
items.summary: What started as one artist’s response to being cut out of a music video has exploded, becoming a driving force in Nigeria’s cultural landscape As a student in the central Nigerian city of Ilorin, Lawal Habeeb Kola loved staying in his hostel room to produce beats rather than returning to his family house in Lagos, the more frenetic city of his birth. In 2022, one of his beats became popular on TikTok, and a version featuring ad-libbed vocals from a hypeman sent it viral. He was invited to the music video shoot in Lagos and thought his big break had finally come, but when the video was released, he was absent.

items.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist in Duran Duran, dies aged 65
items.summary: Musician who had huge 1980s chart success had been diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2018 Duran Duran was transformed by Andy Taylor’s rock edge – and never quite the same without him Andy Taylor – a life in pictures Andy Taylor, the guitarist with 80s pop megastars Duran Duran, has died aged 65. He had been diagnosed with stage four metastatic prostate cancer in 2018, which he disclosed publicly in 2022 when Duran Duran were about to be inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

items.title: Way of the Warrior Kid review - Chris Pratt’s family film is as subtle as a military recruitment video
items.summary: Apple’s tone-deaf Karate Kid knock-off feels like a Maga-approved after-school special It’s hard to avoid the reports that boys and young men are in trouble . Across the US and UK, they’re outpaced by girls on reading tests, are more likely to have behavioral difficulties and exposed to impossible body image standards by the manosphere. You might think that all of this would make you think extra carefully about a film that centers on a 13-year-old boy. Not in the case of Way of the Warrior Kid, a cliche-ridden celebration of machismo and the military that greets the current climate with a shrug. At times, I had to remind myself that I wasn’t watching a Maga-funded after-school special.

items.title: Nasa knocked an asteroid off course. New closeup photos shed light on aftermath
items.summary: Images of Dimorphos four years on from crash could help scientists design potential planetary defence system Humanity may not yet have a means of fending off a Vogon constructor fleet – the destroyers of Earth in The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy – but its prospects of surviving an encounter with a rogue asteroid are looking considerably brighter. Four years after Nasa deliberately slammed a spacecraft into a roughly 160-metre-wide asteroid called Dimorphos to knock it off course, scientists have released the first closeup images of the aftermath.

items.title: Beaver supermoon lights up skylines around the world – video
items.summary: A stunning supermoon rose over skylines around the world. Supermoons occur when the full moon coincides with the moon being at or near its closest point to Earth, making it appear larger than usual. The November full moon is also known as the beaver moon, a name thought to date to when hunters traditionally set traps for beavers in autumn to secure a supply of warm fur for the winter

items.title: The crime-solving surgeon who inspired Sherlock Holmes
items.summary: Sherlock Holmes is one of history's greatest fictional detectives – but his powers of deduction weren't a simple figment of the imagination. In this episode, historian Lindsey Fitzharris introduces listeners to Edinburgh surgeon Joseph Bell, a medical man who used his remarkable powers of observation to diagnose patients, help pioneer modern forensic science… and investigate suspicious deaths.
